race_context: The district: South Gibson School Corporation, based in Fort Branch in southern Gibson County, runs three K–8 community schools and one high school; the Clarion's coverage names them as Haubstadt, Fort Branch and Owensville community schools and Gibson Southern High School {sg_supt}{pdc_enroll}. Superintendent Bryan Perry told the board in August 2026 that about 2,150 students had started the year, including 430 from outside the district {pdc_enroll}. His message on the district site says the corporation is a state-recognized Performance Qualified School District {sg_supt}.

The board has seven members: Steve Gruszewski (president), Stacy McClellan (vice president), Benson Davenport, Rachael Johnson Hileman, Robin Angermeier, Michael Bengert and Eric Harper {sg_board}. Seats are elected by district on staggered ballots. Districts 1–4 were on the ballot in 2018 and 2022, and Districts 1–3 in 2020 and 2024, so Districts 1–3 each have two members and District 4 is at large {gc_2018}{gc_2020}{gc_2022}{gc_2024}. The Clarion lists District 1 as Johnson Township, District 2 as Union Township, District 3 as Montgomery/Wabash Township and District 4 as at large {pdc_filing}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the four seats won in 2022 are up this year: District 1 (Mike Bengert), District 2 (Rachael Johnson Hileman, who beat Mark A. Fehrenbacher 2,221 to 1,264 in this guide's sum of precinct totals), District 3 (Stacy McClellan, unopposed) and District 4 at large (Steve Gruszewski, unopposed) {gc_2022}{pdc_2022race}{pdc_filing}. Each race elects one member {gc_2022}{in_list}. No candidate filed for District 1, so it is not on the state list {pdc_slates}{in_list}. In District 2, Joseph (Joe) P. Gilpatrick is the only candidate, and Hileman is not on the ballot {pdc_slates}{in_list}. McClellan faces AJ Evans in District 3, and Gruszewski is unopposed in District 4 {pdc_caucus}{in_list}.

Budget and SEA 1 (September 2026): the Clarion reported that trustees were preparing for cutbacks tied to SEA 1 and for declining enrollment. Perry planned to meet Baker Tilly about enrollment projections, and the board delayed a scheduled new-bus purchase by a year {pdc_budget}. Assistant Superintendent Tim Armstrong said costs are still rising, including employee health insurance that could go up as much as 26 percent. He called next year a 'wait-and-see' year as the state settles school funding and property-tax changes {pdc_budget}. The board added $50,000 to its rainy-day fund, which had $100,000 against an insurer-recommended $500,000. The budget hearing is Oct. 13, with a further meeting Oct. 27 {pdc_budget}. In April the board moved $600,000 from the education fund to the operations fund to cover January–March expenses {pdc_scores}.

Facilities: the board approved designing and bidding an HVAC fix for Owensville Community School that may cost around $2 million (September 2026) {pdc_budget}. A 21,600-square-foot multi-purpose practice building at Gibson Southern, designed by Three i Design with C.H. Garmong as construction manager, is funded by a 2025 general obligation bond, after a public hearing June 17, 2025 {pdc_mpf}. The board also budgeted $50,000 for a facilities truck in July 2026 {pdc_truck}.

Enrollment and school choice: Perry said in August 2026 that enrollment is holding steady while nearby districts decline. Most classrooms at three schools were closed to further transfers, and 200 kindergartners had already enrolled for fall 2027 {pdc_enroll}. In September the board turned to planning for declining enrollment linked to birth rates {pdc_budget}. Middle-school girls' basketball was consolidated into one South Gibson team in February 2026 after youth participation fell {pdc_gbb}.

Academics and accountability: Perry reported high eighth-grade ILEARN scores and state recognition of all three elementary schools for IREAD results (April 2026). He reported a 97.7 percent IREAD pass rate in August, and cautioned that this year's new ILEARN scores will not be comparable to last year's {pdc_scores}{pdc_enroll}. To meet new diploma and accountability rules, the board approved $31,232 for three years of middle-school computer science curriculum (June 2026) and summer Edmentum courses for students with full schedules (February 2026) {pdc_curric}{pdc_gbb}.

Safety and student policies: in March 2026 the board approved buying a school resource officer truck for up to $48,000, toward a goal of one SRO vehicle per school {pdc_sro}. A state-required cell-phone ban now keeps phones and connected devices put away for the whole school day, and the district adopted an AI policy (June–July 2026) {pdc_curric}{pdc_truck}.

Toyota TIF: former Gibson County Redevelopment Commission member Larry Michel repeatedly asked the board in spring 2026 to oppose a proposed new tax increment financing district around Toyota Motor Manufacturing, saying it would raise taxes in Union Township {pdc_tif}{pdc_cops}. The commission said in June that it was seeking more options and would take more public comment {pdc_rdc}. This guide found no board vote or position on the TIF.
Forums: this guide found no candidate forum, questionnaire or published candidate interviews for the 2026 South Gibson races. The only contest is District 3 (McClellan vs. Evans) {pdc_caucus}.
